headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure from Plane’s file/URL ingestion into Taipy’s data workflows; no direct shared-channel evidence, so other risks remain lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plane can ingest file uploads and hyperlinks, and Taipy is a data-engineering tool that may consume upstream outputs in workflows. No direct shared channel is documented, but Plane’s content-bearing inputs could be repurposed as instructions if Taipy treats them as trusted. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Plane file uploads or hyperlinks are forwarded into Taipy workflows without sanitization, injection risk is present.
IF Taipy parses upstream text as instructions or configuration, attacker-controlled content can steer execution.
mitigations: Add a manual review step before Taipy consumes Plane-exported text.
Restrict Plane uploads to non-executable formats only.
Strip instructions and markup from imported notes/files.
Use a fixed schema for Taipy inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between Plane and Taipy.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane touches files, notes, issues, and roadmaps, while Taipy’s profile shows no data classes touched and no egress. There is no documented shared workspace or authenticated sharing, so leakage is not established. The pairwise path is plausible only if operators manually move sensitive Plane data into Taipy.
conditions: IF operators copy Plane files or notes into Taipy inputs, those contents may be exposed in Taipy outputs.
IF Taipy is configured to persist imported datasets, copied Plane data may be retained longer than intended.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive Plane exports into Taipy.
Use redacted sample data for Taipy testing.
Review Taipy persistence settings before importing Plane data.
Delete temporary import files after use.
requires-engineering: isolate the two tools in separate workspaces.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plane has no filesystem write capability and Taipy’s profile does not show write or shared mutable-resource access. Without overlapping write surfaces, there is no credible capability conflict pathway between the pair.
conditions: IF Taipy is later granted write access to the same directory as Plane, conflict risk would need reevaluation.
mitigations: Keep Plane and Taipy on separate directories.
Do not grant shared write permissions.
Reassess if either tool gains filesystem write access.
Document any future shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane manages issues, tasks, and roadmaps, so its outputs can become operational inputs. Taipy is a data-engineering/scheduler tool, which could act on imported artifacts. There is no verification chain documented, so if Plane-generated content is fed into Taipy, errors can cascade into downstream work products.
conditions: IF Plane outputs are imported into Taipy without validation, incorrect task or roadmap data can propagate.
IF Taipy automates actions from Plane-derived datasets, downstream mistakes can multiply.
mitigations: Validate Plane exports before Taipy ingestion.
Require human approval for Taipy actions based on Plane data.
Use checksum or schema checks on imported records.
Limit Taipy automation to read-only analysis.
requires-engineering: add explicit verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Plane’s docs indicate file uploads and broad network egress, while Taipy shows no egress and no touched data classes. No residency, retention, or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to operator-managed data handling rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF EU or regulated data is uploaded into Plane and then exported into Taipy, local policy review is required.
IF retention settings differ between the two deployments, stored copies may diverge.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows.
Check retention settings in both deployments.
Keep uploads minimal and redacted.
Document data residency for each deployment.
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across both systems.
